Although recent progress has been largely driven by artificial intelligence, current manufacturing intelligence often remains external to physical systems and suffers from limited robustness, interpretability, and transferability in complex industrial environments. Here, we present a unified perspective on smart manufacturing through the framework of artificial intelligence (AI), embodied intelligence (EI), and physical intelligence (PI). AI provides abstraction, prediction, and generative capability; EI enables closed-loop perception, decision-making, and physical interaction; and PI embeds adaptive intelligence directly into materials, structures, and physicochemical processes. We further discuss how generative intelligence is beginning to connect these domains through inverse design, adaptive fabrication, and physics-constrained behavior realization. Recent advances in collaborative robotics, embodied digital twins, self-optimizing production systems, and physically intelligent materials, including self-actuating, self-healing, multistable, and shape-morphing systems, are reviewed. Finally, we propose an integrated AI-EI-PI framework spanning the full manufacturing lifecycle, highlighting a transition toward manufacturing systems in which intelligence is increasingly co-designed across algorithms, embodied agents, and matter itself.\", \"doi\": \"10.1002/advs.78384\", \"pmid\": \"42932218\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13703982\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.1002/advs.78384\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \…

model as most of the prior works do. We consider a standard mat hematical formu-

ﬁnd a policy so that it is consistently preferred by the KL-re gularized preference

Abstract
To use reinforcement learning from human feed-
back (RLHF) in practical applications, it is cru-
cial to learn reward models from diverse sources
of human feedback and to consider human factors
involved in providing feedback of different types.
However, the systematic study of learning from
diverse types of feedback is held back by limited
standardized tooling available to researchers. To
bridge this gap, we proposeRLHF-Blender, a con-
figurable, interactive interface for learning from
human feedback. RLHF-Blender provides a mod-
ular experimentation framework and implemen-
tation that enables researchers to systematically
investigate the properties and qualities of human
feedback for reward learning. The system facil-
itates the exploration of various feedback types,
including demonstrations, rankings, comparisons,
and natural language instructions, as well as stud-
ies considering the impact of human factors on
their effectiveness. We discuss a set of concrete
research opportunities enabled by RLHF-Blender.
More information is available at our website.
